name: Stefan Dušan Crowned Emperor of the Serbs and Greeks
summary: Stefan Dušan, king of Serbia, is crowned 'Emperor of the Serbs and Greeks' at Skopje on Easter 1346, establishing a patriarchate for the Serbian Orthodox Church simultanuously. At its peak, his realm controls most of the Balkan peninsula except Constantinople and Thessaloniki: Albania, Epirus, Macedonia, Thessaly, and much of Greece. Dušan promulgates the Zakonik (Law Code, 1349), a comprehensive legal code modeled partly on Byzantine law that defines medieval Serbian governance. He dreams of conquering Constantinople itself.

_quarry.structural_significance: The peak of Serbian imperial power; Dušan's sudden death in 1355 without a capable successor causes immediate fragmentation; the weakened Serbian state is unable to resist Ottoman expansion, leading to Kosovo (1389); Dušan's imperial title and legal code establish the juridical and symbolic vocabulary of Serbian national identity for centuries
